thread:
Nina: Heads-up — our token-level latency dashboard is spiking for /chat/stream. Token tail (p99 token-to-token) up ~4x since 03:10 UTC. https://dash.redwood/internal/latency/token-level

Raj: I see the same. Burn rate for p95 crossed >3 for two back-to-back 5m windows. The old alert metric is static so it didn't page. @oncall can you check? :eyes:

Maria: Traces look interesting — KV cache hit rate dropped from ~98% -> ~75% at ~03:12 UTC. Also saw kernel_selection flip to fallback_float path on a subset of GPUs around that time. Possible kernel-picker regression in last runtime deploy (rev r-2026-03-10).

Kevin: Can you paste the PromQL you used to compute burn rate? I'll add an anomaly detector and a short-term smoothing to the dashboard.

Maria: ```promql
# approx p95 token latency per token for /chat/stream
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/chat/stream"}[5m])) by (le))
```

Raj: Quick alert draft (wip):
```yaml
name: runtime.token.p95_burnrate
expr: increase(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/chat/stream"}[5m])) by (le))[5m]) > 2.5
for: 5m
labels: {severity: page}
```

Nina: Let's not page on every blip — we get noisy pages during cache warmup. Proposal: page only if (burn_rate_p95 > 2.5 AND kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.15) OR (anomaly_score_ewma > 6). That keeps pages for real regressions.

sre-bot: deploy: runtime/kernel-picker r-2026-03-11 applied to cluster runtime-prod at 03:08 UTC (by deploy-bot)

Kevin: We should emit kernel_selector_decision metric (labels: model, kernel_family, decision) so we can correlate sudden kernel-family shifts. Filed INF-2345 to add the metric and dashboard panel.

Maria: Profiling notes (flamegraph -> https://perf.redwood/profiles/1799500000): extra time is in kernel memcpy + launch overhead when kernel_family=="fallback" — ~30% of the regression. KV cache misses account for the rest (increased backend fetches).

Raj: Action items: 1) revert kernel-picker sticky policy to previous (24h stick) as a short-term mitigation, 2) add kv cache shard-level telemetry (kv_cache_shard_miss_rate), 3) update alert rule to combine burn-rate + kv miss + anomaly detector. Owners?

Nina: I'll take 1 & 3. I'll stage the alert change (canary to runtime-canary route) and run a 30m observation. Kevin takes #2.

oncall: Acked. If it pages after the new rule is live, page SRE oncall (@pagerduty) immediately. I'll monitor until Nina confirms canary is stable. :white_check_mark:

Nina: Plan for longer-term: (a) add a per-route batching-heuristic KPI (avg batch size, batch latency) to correlate tiny batches causing kernel fallback; (b) add a burn-rate anomaly alert using MAD/EWMA to reduce false positives. Filing tickets for both.

Kevin: I'll also instrument kernel selection histograms and per-device memcpy times so we can build a machine-learned selector in future.

Raj: Great. I'll update the incident playbook to include these combined conditions and add a runbook snippet with PromQL examples and rollback steps.

Nina: Thanks team — let's regroup in 45m after the canary. :thumbsup:
